query:
With respect to Overhead System Renewal:
a) Please update Figures 3,4, 7, 8, 13, 14, 21, 22, 26 and 27 with 2023 information.
b) [p.9] Please provide a revised version of Table 4 that includes 2017 ACA information, as
well as 2029 ACA information based on the proposed investments included in the DSP.
Please provide in Excel format.
c) [p.25-26] Please provide a version of the information included in each of Figures 24 and 25
in tabular format, that also includes 2017 ACA information, as well as the 2029 ACA
information based on the proposed investments included in the DSP. Please provide in
Excel format. e. [p.34] Please provide a breakdown of annual costs included in Table 7
based on the asset class included in Table 8.
d) [p.37] Please provide a similar table as Table 9 that shows the volume of assets replaced
each year as part of the Overhead Infrastructure Resilience segment.
e) [p.34] Please provide a breakdown of annual costs included in Table 7 based on the asset
class included in Table 8.
answer:
The filings don't let me produce most of what you asked for. I could fully answer only part (d). The rest are requests for new analysis or an Excel file, and I can't create files or run Toronto Hydro's models. Below is what the filings do contain for each item. All page references are to Exhibit 2B, Section E6.5 (the Distribution System Plan chapter), unless I say otherwise.

**a) Figures 3, 4, 7, 8, 13, 14, 21, 22, 26 and 27 updated with 2023 data**
- These figures plot data to 2022 (for example, Figures 21 and 22 cover customers interrupted and customer hours interrupted for overhead switches, 2018–2022) [cite:rds-823164:387].
- The filings I can access don't contain 2023 versions of these figures. The figures are charts, and I did not find their underlying data in the text I retrieved. I can't update them.
- The ACA update report covers year-end 2017, year-end 2022 and projections to 2029 [cite:rds-823163:384]. It does not include 2023 results.

**b) Table 4 (wood pole condition) with 2017 and 2029-with-investment columns**
The filed Table 4 gives pole counts by Health Index (HI) band for 2022 and for 2029 without investment [cite:rds-823164:373]:

| Band | 2022 | 2029 (no investment) |
|---|---|---|
| HI1 | 68,193 | 60,253 |
| HI2 | 7,536 | 8,310 |
| HI3 | 21,015 | 5,544 |
| HI4 | 8,918 | 24,404 |
| HI5 | 504 | 7,655 |

- The ACA update report says it produces 2017 year-end results "for convenience" [cite:rds-823163:384]. I did not find the 2017 band counts in the text I retrieved.
- I did not find a 2029 projection that includes the planned DSP investments. The filing states only that about 30% of wood poles are forecast to show material deterioration by 2029 without intervention [cite:rds-823164:366].
- I can't build the Excel file.

**c) Tabular versions of Figures 24 and 25 (gang-operated and SCADA-Mate switch condition)**
- These two figures are bar charts of HI1–HI5 switch counts for 2022 and 2029 without investment [cite:rds-823164:389].
- The retrieved text has axis labels only, not the underlying values. I also did not find 2017 or 2029-with-investment values.
- I can't produce the tables or the Excel file.

**d) A Table 9-style table for Overhead Infrastructure Resiliency volumes**
- The filings do not provide this table. Table 9 covers only the Overhead System Renewal segment. Its forecast volumes are in the table below [cite:rds-823164:399].
- For the Resiliency segment, the filing says "the total number and timing of the areas targeted will depend on the specific locations and required scope... (which have not yet been determined)" [cite:rds-823164:400].
- The filing gives only forecast costs for the segment: $11.4M in 2026, $24.1M in 2027, $24.8M in 2028 and $25.6M in 2029, with nothing in 2025 [cite:rds-823164:397, cite:rds-823164:400]. It also gives one example from a past project, Carlingview Drive [cite:rds-823164:400].
- Toronto Hydro would need to supply the per-year asset volumes.

| Asset class (Table 9, Overhead System Renewal) | 2025 | 2026 | 2027 | 2028 | 2029 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Poles | 2,113 | 1,556 | 1,556 | 1,556 | 1,556 | 8,337 |
| Transformers | 1,232 | 907 | 911 | 908 | 889 | 4,847 |
| OH switches | 123 | 91 | 91 | 104 | 102 | 511 |
| Conductors (km, primary cables only) | 66 | 49 | 49 | 45 | 44 | 253 |

**e) Annual costs in Table 7 broken down by the asset classes in Table 8**
- The filings contain no such breakdown.
- Table 7 gives only segment totals, in $ millions [cite:rds-823164:398]:

| Year | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 | 2027 | 2028 | 2029 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost ($M) | 36.1 | 38.2 | 38.2 | 32.5 | 73.9 | 50.5 | 49.4 | 53.3 | 60.3 | 58.9 |

- Table 8 gives 2020–2024 volumes by asset class [cite:rds-823164:398]:

| Asset class | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Poles | 1,418 | 1,263 | 1,137 | 790 | 2,674 | 7,282 |
| Transformers | 401 | 584 | 579 | 215 | 1,892 | 3,671 |
| OH switches | 185 | 290 | 71 | 43 | 114 | 703 |
| Conductors (km) | 53.0 | 60.0 | 76.0 | 4.8 | 45.1 | 238.8 |

- The filing says the 2025–2029 forecast is built from historical unit-cost trends and forecast volumes by asset class [cite:rds-823164:399]. It does not publish the unit costs or the cost split.
- Allocating costs by asset class would need Toronto Hydro's own cost data. I won't estimate it.

These items (a, b, c and e) look like undertakings for Toronto Hydro to answer, because they depend on data and model runs outside the filings. I can draft the wording of those requests if you'd like.

judge.rationale: The candidate's 2022 and 2029 (without investment) wood pole figures for Table 4 match the reference. However, it leaves out the 2017 ACA values, the switch condition tables, the 2023 figure updates, the Resiliency replacement volumes (1,235 poles, 333 transformers, etc.) and the cost breakdown by asset class, all of which the reference provides. It also repeats filed transformer pacing and 2020–2024 volumes that the reference corrects as administrative errors.
